From 0f0c6415af409d213e7a132390a850c1251b92ef Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 From: Akira Ajisaka Date: Tue, 10 May 2016 10:02:46 -0700 Subject: [PATCH] HADOOP-13118. Fix IOUtils#cleanup and IOUtils#closeStream javadoc. Contributed by Wei-Chiu Chuang. diff --git a/hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/io/IOUtils.java b/hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/io/IOUtils.java index 2588bf1f465..e6749b76bfa 100644 --- a/hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/io/IOUtils.java +++ b/hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/io/IOUtils.java @@ -234,7 +234,7 @@ public static void skipFully(InputStream in, long len) throws IOException { } /** - * Close the Closeable objects and ignore any {@link IOException} or + * Close the Closeable objects and ignore any {@link Throwable} or * null pointers. Must only be used for cleanup in exception handlers. * * @param log the log to record problems to at debug level. Can be null. @@ -255,7 +255,7 @@ public static void cleanup(Log log, java.io.Closeable... closeables) { } /** - * Closes the stream ignoring {@link IOException}. + * Closes the stream ignoring {@link Throwable}. * Must only be called in cleaning up from exception handlers. * * @param stream the Stream to close -- 2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: IOUtils.java**
   - **Line 238**: The Javadoc comment for the `cleanup` method was modified to change the wording from "ignore any {@link IOException}" to "ignore any {@link Throwable}". This broadens the scope of exceptions that are ignored during cleanup.
   - **Line 259**: The Javadoc comment for the `closeStream` method was similarly modified to change "ignoring {@link IOException}" to "ignoring {@link Throwable}", again expanding the types of exceptions that can be ignored when closing streams.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications in the `IOUtils.java` file are related in that they both update the Javadoc comments for methods that handle resource cleanup. By changing the references from `IOException` to `Throwable`, the patch clarifies that these methods can now ignore a wider range of exceptions, not just IO-related ones. This change enhances the robustness of the cleanup operations by allowing them to handle more types of errors gracefully.

Here is the root cause: The original implementation of the `cleanup` and `closeStream` methods only ignored `IOException`, which could lead to unhandled exceptions if other types of `Throwable` were thrown during the cleanup process. This could result in resource leaks or incomplete cleanup operations, especially in scenarios where non-IO exceptions occur. The patch addresses this by broadening the exception handling to include all `Throwable` types, ensuring that all potential exceptions are ignored during cleanup.
